title: Deform
tagline: Put a part modelled flat onto a curved profile the way a real layer bends. Every vertex, edge and face goes through one map; small gaps between faces are repaired, up to a limit you set.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Parts modelled flat must sit on the curved ski, and native Bend flexes only around an axis. Deform carries every point of a part from a From chain to a To chain, so it follows rocker and camber like a real layer. Small gaps between faces are repaired so the result can usually be enclosed, offset or thickened.
useWhen: An insert, core or protector modelled flat
Features that must follow rocker and camber
A whole body, or only some faces
slides.caption: A 100 x 5 block bent onto an R600 bend: the side on the chain stays 100 long; the side 5 toward the centre is 99.2.

slides.title: Four rules to predict the result

points.head: 1. Distance along is kept
points.body: A point s along the From reference lands s along the To reference.

points.head: 2. Height and width are kept
points.body: 5 mm above the From chain lands 5 mm above the To chain.

points.head: 3. Layers shrink inside, stretch outside
points.body: Inside = the circle's centre side. At height h: (R - h)/R inside, (R + h)/R outside.

points.head: 4. Square faces stay flat
points.body: Faces square to the chain stay planes; faces parallel to it curve with it.

slides.title: Using it: get the side right

points.head: Inside is the centre side
points.body: Layers on the inside of a bend shrink, on the outside they stretch.

points.head: Flip normal
points.body: Result on the wrong side of the profile (upside-down)? Tick it.

points.head: Flip
points.body: Running the wrong way along the profile? Tick the arrow beside To edge(s).

points.head: Both chains in one plane? Binormal
points.body: You pick a direction square to that plane (a face, mate connector or axis); 'up' stays fixed in the plane. Not for chains that wander in 3D.

points.head: Otherwise Frenet (default)
points.body: 'Up' comes from the chain's own bend and is carried along smoothly. After an inflection (the bend changes direction) it points away from the new centre; Flip normal puts the part right.

points.head: Kept and changed
points.body: Kept: distance along, height, width. Changed: lengths at other heights, angles, areas. On planar chains end and side faces stay planes; faces parallel to the chain become freeform.

points.head: How accurate
points.body: Edges aim for 0.5 um, faces for 2 um (micrometres; a hair is about 70 um). Repaired faces move up to the Seam repair limit (default 50 um).

points.head: Face count
points.body: It can drop: tiny faces are absorbed. Ski top 78 -> 75 faces; a lid 193 -> 185.

slides.title: Result: flat boxes and their deformed copies

cards.head: Flat below, deformed above
cards.body: The test studio: boxes bent onto an R300 quarter arc. The sources stay; each result is a new body named with the suffix.

cards.head: Real models
cards.body: Ski top surface: 78 faces, 30 free edges (edges with a face on one side only: the outer boundary) -> 75 faces, 30 free edges. A 193-face lid: 54 free edges -> 54, 185 faces. Same free edges = no new openings.

keys: One per source body, named with the suffix (the test boxes: 'Box A (D1)', 'Box B (D1)'). The source stays. A solid is closed back into a solid where possible.

items.head: New face identities
items.body: A refilled face is a new face. A saved selection (Move face, Mutual trim, Enclose) may say '1 missing selection': pick it again.

items.head: Thick parts on tight bends
items.body: A layer higher than the radius folds inside-out and Deform does not warn you. Keep every height below the tightest inside radius.

items.head: Big bodies
items.body: A feature shares about 24,000 mapped points between its bodies (at least 110 per face). Very large bodies can stop with 'Too many steps': deform fewer bodies per feature or raise Mapped surface accuracy.

items.head: Seam repair limit
items.body: Leave it at 50 um. Raise it only when the feature names the value and the shift is acceptable. Up to 40 repair attempts per body.

items.head: 3D chains
items.body: Frenet fixes 'up' once per chain, at its first edge that is not straight. If the part is on the wrong side, try Flip normal.

slides.title: Under the hood: how a face is rebuilt

points.head: Sample, map, fit
points.body: The face is sampled on a grid, every point goes through the map, and a smooth surface (a B-spline: a smooth curved surface made from a net of control points) is fitted through the moved points.

points.head: Refine, trim
points.body: Where it misses the exact map by more than Mapped surface accuracy (2 um) the grid gets denser; then it is cut to the mapped outline.

points.head: Planes stay planes
points.body: A face that maps flat (within 2 um) is built as a true plane. Faces with holes or wrapping outlines are filled from their outline instead.

slides.title: Under the hood: seams and the repair

points.head: Why a gap remains
points.body: Faces are fitted one by one and miss by a few um; the kernel (Onshape's geometry engine) joins only about 1 um. Faces that meet but are not joined: an unsewn seam.

points.head: The repair
points.body: The smaller face is refilled from its neighbours' exact edges and joined, and kept only if it stays within the Seam repair limit and really joins.

points.head: The limit
points.body: Default 50 um, maximum 200 um. Raise it only if the faces that move are not sealing, mating or datum faces.
